hook: SCP-5320 is a snailfish with no visible head or tail, and the drones following it have yet to find an end. It is a Keter, but this is a comedy. The containment procedures list its honorific titles and require snack offerings on the break-room microwave, and the logs that follow show a research team that has clearly had a lot of time on its hands.
whyItMatters:
This entry shows how far an article can get on tone alone. The anomaly itself barely does anything; the entertainment comes from the staff around it, and the clinical report format makes their mock devotion funnier by recording it with a straight face.

It also plays with a familiar expectation in the genre: when personnel start behaving strangely around an object, readers assume a mental effect. The article builds that suspicion on purpose so it can answer it later.
thingsToNotice:
The escalation is the fun part. Greetings like praising the Fish become prayers about snacks and soda, a staff meeting opens with a ritual response and debates whether the Fish could tie up the Christian God's legs, and the holiday gathering is christened the first annual Fishmas. By the time an email from Dr. Keul is signed as High Priestess of the church, it really does look like an infohazard.

The investigating agent concludes it was a false alarm: just an elaborate running joke among bored staff, which Keul promises to tone down. The final sting comes in her own note, where she grumbles about a coworker moving her wizard figure and dreads another 69 years of bad luck, showing that the urge to invent superstitions does not stop at Marine Research Installation 14.
